original.q: Near the Sun itself, what surprising color can a Martian sunset have?
original.d: Fine dust lets blue light remain concentrated near the setting Sun, while much of the surrounding sky looks yellow or orange.
original.evidence: NASA explains the blue glow near the Sun in Mars sunset images.

replacement: Why can Earth’s upper atmosphere give off a faint glow on a dark night, even away from an aurora?

original.q: Fresh black lava at Tanzania’s Ol Doinyo Lengai can soon change to which color?
original.d: Its unusual carbonate-rich lava reacts with water after eruption, changing the appearance of the cooled flows.
original.evidence: USGS says fresh black flows turn white through reactions as they absorb water.

replacement: In a laboratory water channel, one sand dune pushed another farther away without touching it. What carried the interaction?

original.q: Sea-ice “frost flowers” grow when water vapor does what?
original.d: The delicate crystals form on the ice surface without first becoming liquid droplets.
original.s: National Snow and Ice Data Center
choices: Melts old snow into branching channels
original.evidence: NSIDC defines frost flowers as direct vapor-to-solid crystal growth.

replacement: What evidence showed that Old Faithful once stopped erupting long enough for a very different landscape to develop on its mound?

original.q: What ingredient from smoldering vegetation can combine with moist air to create visibility-destroying superfog?
original.d: Smoke and moisture from damp, smoldering material mix with cool, nearly saturated air, producing exceptionally dense fog.
original.evidence: NWS specifies smoke and moisture from smoldering organic material mixed with cool saturated air.

replacement: How can polar observers sometimes see a distorted image of the Sun while it is still well below the horizon?

original.q: Which process helps an eruption cloud build the electrical charge needed for volcanic lightning?
original.d: Fragmentation and interactions among ash particles can separate charge; ice and water processes can contribute higher in the plume.
choices: Radioactive minerals emitting a directed current
Sulfur gases reacting with atmospheric ozone
Lava cooling into naturally magnetized rock
original.evidence: USGS describes plume particle processes, fragmentation and hydrometeors as charging mechanisms.

replacement: The ocean floor has a magnetic pattern resembling paired zebra stripes. What history does it record?

original.q: On some desert pavements, fine soil accumulates where in relation to the close-packed surface stones?
original.d: Windblown dust can enter and build the fine soil horizon beneath the stony surface, rather than simply burying it.
choices: Only on top of the stones
In separate dunes beyond the pavement
original.evidence: BLM describes the wind-deposited fine-particle horizon directly beneath desert pavement.

replacement: Why can melting Greenland ice make sea level fall nearby while raising it far away?

original.q: Which familiar unpleasant smell did Rosetta scientists associate with hydrogen sulfide detected at comet 67P?
original.d: The comet’s gases contain several pungent compounds. This comparison describes the detected chemistry, not an astronaut actually sniffing the coma.
original.evidence: ESA’s ROSINA account specifically associates cometary hydrogen sulfide with rotten eggs.

replacement: What gives many glacier-fed lakes their milky turquoise color?

original.q: Saturn’s diffuse E ring gets fresh icy material from what ongoing source?
original.d: Some plume particles escape the moon and join the broad ring; much of the ejected material falls back as snow.
choices: Ice swept in from passing comets
original.evidence: NASA identifies Enceladus’s plumes as an E-ring source and describes fallback snow.

replacement: What warms the surprisingly mild deep water of Antarctica’s ice-covered Lake Vanda?

original.q: The dome-shaped “volcanoes” discovered off Santa Barbara were built from what unusual flow material?
original.d: Heavy petroleum seeped out and piled into underwater mounds. These are not magma-fed volcanoes.
original.evidence: USGS identifies the flows as asphalt or tar and explicitly distinguishes them from true volcanoes.

replacement: A thin slab of itacolumite can do what surprising thing without first being melted?

original.q: What repeatedly failed to unleash the enormous Ice Age floods from Glacial Lake Missoula?
original.d: Glacial ice blocked the Clark Fork drainage. When the barrier gave way, huge volumes of lake water escaped across the Pacific Northwest.
original.evidence: NPS attributes the lake and catastrophic floods to an ice dam and its failure.

replacement: Huge parallel ridges at Montana’s Camas Prairie were recognized as giant versions of what familiar water-made pattern?
